title: Quiz: Generalised Linear Models — Logistic and Poisson Regression

questions.text: In logistic regression, what does add_predictions(mod, type = 'response') return for each observation?
questions.explanation: type = 'response' applies the inverse link function (logistic function) to the linear predictor, transforming log-odds into probabilities between 0 and 1.

questions.text: A Poisson regression coefficient of 0.05 for 'age' means that each additional year of age increases the expected count by 5 units.
questions.explanation: Poisson coefficients are on the log scale. exp(0.05) ≈ 1.051 — each additional year multiplies the expected count by 1.051, a 5.1% multiplicative increase, not an additive increase of 5 units.

questions.text: Why can't ordinary linear regression (OLS) be directly used for a binary 0/1 response?
options: OLS requires the response to be a count variable
OLS can predict values outside [0, 1] which are not valid probabilities
OLS requires all predictors to be categorical
OLS cannot handle large datasets efficiently
questions.explanation: OLS is unconstrained — it can predict negative values or values greater than 1. These are not valid probabilities. Logistic regression constrains predictions to (0,1) via the logistic link function.

questions.text: In glm(), which family argument fits a logistic regression model for a binary outcome?
questions.explanation: Logistic regression uses the binomial family with the logit link. The binomial family models proportions/counts of successes; the logit link maps probabilities to the real line.

questions.text: An exponentiated logistic regression coefficient for 'toptier' is 7.0. Which interpretation is correct?
options: Top-tier students have a 7-unit higher probability of admission
Top-tier students are 7 times more likely to be admitted in absolute terms
Attending a top-tier school multiplies the odds of admission by 7
Top-tier students have 7% higher admission rates
questions.explanation: Exponentiated logistic coefficients are odds ratios. OR = 7 means the odds of admission for top-tier school students are 7 times the odds for non-top-tier students. This is not a direct statement about probability differences.
